_steward_hook: Records this worktree, then prints the board. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-steward-coordination-design.md
🔴 `worktree 2>&1 1>/dev/null` IS DELIBERATE AND THE ORDER MATTERS. stderr carries the
NOTICES (HEAD moved here since the last session; another session was last seen here), which
are the entire point of the marker. stdout carries only the canonical scope, which exists for
scripting and which `who` prints on the next line anyway. `2>&1` first duplicates stderr onto
the terminal, THEN `1>/dev/null` silences stdout. Writing `>/dev/null 2>&1` instead throws the
notices away and leaves a hook that does nothing visible.
⚠ Both commands fail open and the whole thing is `|| true`: a session must never fail to start
because the steward was unreachable. 5s timeout covers two ~0.4s round trips.

hooks.command: [ -d backend/node_modules ] && { node backend/scripts/steward.mjs worktree 2>&1 1>/dev/null; node backend/scripts/steward.mjs who 2>&1; } || true
